audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 95837) idled in an open transaction for 4 seconds, holding locks that blocked checkout and degraded success to 54% against a 95% SLO. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian initially requested a change-calendar check (Invariant I2), which returned no active window, then accepted. The authority authorized termination, the executor killed the session, and the verifier confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits and 100% checkout success over 10 seconds. Total negotiation and execution took 92 seconds, well within the 60-second business tolerance once the decision was made.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch job (batch_replayable_inventory) held locks while idle in transaction, blocking checkout sessions.
lessons: Pre-load change-calendar evidence for inventory_reconcile in the guardian runbook so the Continuity Guardian can satisfy Invariant I2 without an extra probe round.
Add a lock-timeout or idle-in-transaction watchdog for batch_replayable_inventory workers to auto-terminate after a few seconds and avoid manual negotiation.
Instrument inventory_reconcile to emit its checkpoint progress to the workload registry, enabling the trade-off calculator to use actual remaining runtime instead of the ~896s estimate.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian reused the same evidence set in Round 2 without incorporating the newly fetched change-calendar result, forcing the Continuity Guardian to re-evaluate identical data; the Continuity Guardian correctly enforced Invariant I2 but could have pre-fetched the calendar in parallel with the registry probe.
follow_ups: Update the inventory-platform runbook to include change-calendar lookup steps for inventory_reconcile.
Deploy a pg_idle_in_transaction_timeout or equivalent guard for batch_worker role.
Extend the workload registry schema to accept real-time checkpoint offsets from inventory_reconcile.
